Ahri.combo: After rooting Ahri with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks. If Ahri R Spirit Rush is down, use Neeko P Inherent Glamour to disguise yourself as an ally who isn’t visible, then approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom. Root Ahri with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so your landing hits her.
Ahri.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Ahri’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first, but withstand the true damage from Ahri Q Orb of Deception with your health pool. If healing from Ahri P Essence Theft can undo your burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Ahri.escape: The moment after Ahri E Charm is used is your chance to close in.
Ahri.fight: If there’s no good angle to hit with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don’t force the cast; poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Immediately after dodging Ahri E Charm or while Ahri R Spirit Rush is down, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and deal damage.
Ahri.laning: With a minion wave between you, Ahri E Charm can’t reach you. Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows, travels faster, and roots longer when it passes through minions, so look for an angle across the wave. If Neeko Q Blooming Burst hits both the wave and Ahri, you can clear the wave and poke at the same time.
Ahri.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Ahri.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Ahri has used Ahri E Charm or is caught by an ally’s engage. Approaching while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour can hide Neeko R Pop Blossom’s windup, but if you go in alone first, you can be caught while preparing it.
Ahri.watch: If Ahri E Charm hits you, she can follow up with her combo, so dodge with a minion between you. Ahri Q Orb of Deception can hit on the return as well, so move outside its return path even after dodging the first pass. The return damage is true damage and cannot be reduced by magic resistance.

Alistar.laning: Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle through minions to aim for a longer, easier-to-hit root. If there’s no angle, use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered basic attack on the enemy while you wait. Watch for Alistar’s engage after missing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Alistar.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Alistar’s damage is mostly magic, so build magic resistance first. If the healing from Alistar P Triumphant Roar can undo Neeko’s burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Alistar.combo: The basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks. After Alistar W Headbutt is used, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko R Pop Blossom hits him when Neeko lands.
Alistar.escape: The moment after Alistar W Headbutt is used is your chance to close the gap. If Alistar Q Pulverize is also down, approach with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so he can’t escape.
Alistar.fight: While Alistar Q Pulverize and Alistar W Headbutt are available, don’t force an engage; poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Once both are down, root Alistar with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then deal damage with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don’t commit your damage; back off and fight again after it ends.
Alistar.phase: In the late game, Neeko becomes weaker after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Alistar.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally’s engage. While Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don’t spend your abilities on Alistar; target the damage dealers behind him. If you can’t retreat, interrupt his engage with fresh crowd control from Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or Neeko R Pop Blossom after he activates his ultimate.
Alistar.watch: Keep your distance to avoid Alistar W Headbutt’s dash and displacement, followed by the knock-up from Alistar Q Pulverize and the stun from Alistar E Trample. Near a turret, don’t give Alistar room to get behind Neeko and push her under it.

Naafiri.watch: If Naafiri Q Darkin Daggers hits you once and applies a bleed, keep your distance until it ends to avoid the second hit. Naafiri E Eviscerate revives her pack, so be careful with your damage right after she uses it until you've cleared the pack. Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit dashes to a targeted champion, so don't roam alone; after an ally dies, retreat and watch for consecutive dashes.
Naafiri.build: Naafiri deals mostly physical damage and Neeko has low armor, so start with Cloth Armor to survive. Choose Plated Steelcaps for boots to increase your armor. If the healing from Naafiri Q Darkin Daggers and Naafiri E Eviscerate is enough to interfere with finishing her off, buy Morellonomicon between your core items.
Naafiri.combo: The basic order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → empowered attack. While Naafiri W The Call of the Pack is active, she can't be targeted, so finish her off after it ends. For an ultimate engage, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, then prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom and catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally's crowd control to land it.
Naafiri.escape: Don't engage just because either Naafiri Q Darkin Daggers or Naafiri E Eviscerate is down. She can escape with multiple movement options, so look for an opening especially before Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit comes back up. Then close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Naafiri.fight: Use Naafiri's melee range to keep your distance and chip away at her health with the empowered attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Once Naafiri E Eviscerate is down and you've cleared her pack again, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and deal a short burst of damage. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, Naafiri has an opening to engage, so stop fighting and create distance.
Naafiri.laning: Farm from behind the minion line to deny Naafiri E Eviscerate an angle to close the gap. Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst after landing E so the explosions chain. If you don't have an angle for the root, wait while using the empowered third attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter on Naafiri.
Naafiri.phase: Watch especially for Naafiri's roams in mid game by setting up vision farther out, and group up to avoid being caught alone in the late game.
Naafiri.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Naafiri is caught by an ally's engage or root. Clear Naafiri's pack with AoE damage like Neeko Q Blooming Burst, aiming for the moment right after Naafiri E Eviscerate revives it. While Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit is available, don't get isolated; move with your allies.

Lulu.escape: Lulu has no dash, but Lulu W Whimsy can shut down Neeko’s engage while it’s available. Engage after it’s used on another ally. If Lulu R Wild Growth is still available, target Lulu herself or someone else instead of the protected target.
Lulu.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Lulu deals magic damage, so magic resistance helps more than armor. When choosing more resistance later, also consider the damage type of the target Lulu is protecting.
Lulu.combo: The basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with a basic attack.
Lulu.fight: Lulu is good at stopping a major engage, so start by steadily poking with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. After Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally, close the distance and look for a chance to root Lulu with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the extra damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, and if there’s no good angle to hit, save it and poke with the third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Lulu.phase: In the late game, Neeko becomes less effective after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Lulu.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally’s engage. Don’t go in alone while Lulu W Whimsy is available. If Lulu R Wild Growth is still available, avoid focusing your attacks on the protected target.
Lulu.watch: Lulu W Whimsy silences you so you can’t cast spells, and it also stops your attacks, so don’t engage with Neeko R Pop Blossom while this spell is available. Lulu R Wild Growth increases its target’s health and knocks up nearby enemies, so be careful about engaging to kill a protected target in one burst.

Janna.phase: Neeko has low armor early, so don’t force trades against targets protected by Janna’s shield. In the late game, Neeko runs out of options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage even more carefully.
Janna.build: Early on, withstand Janna’s damage with a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Janna deals mostly magic damage, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If Janna R Monsoon heals enough to undo a single burst of damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Janna.combo: Transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root the target with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land the ultimate. Use this combo after Janna E Eye Of The Storm is down to avoid wasting burst damage on its shield.
Janna.escape: After Janna Q Howling Gale misses is your chance to engage. If Janna R Monsoon has also been used, the risk of being knocked away is lower, so look for an angle to catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and land Neeko R Pop Blossom. If Janna W Zephyr slows you, don’t force the chase; use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s stealth and movement speed.
Janna.fight: Don’t commit burst damage to a target with Janna E Eye Of The Storm; engage after its shield is down or target someone else. Root the target with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks.
Janna.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to aim for a hit and a long root. If there’s no angle, don’t force it; poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Pressure the ally Janna is protecting to make her use Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then take the initiative if Janna Q Howling Gale and Janna W Zephyr miss.
Janna.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally’s engage. If Janna is behind an allied damage dealer, your engage is easy to knock back, so secure vision and look for a moment when Janna is isolated. Also consider fighting with your back to a wall so it’s easier to re-engage if Janna R Monsoon knocks you away.
Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale can knock Neeko up and interrupt her engage. If you hear the tornado from outside vision, dodge its path, and don’t rush your engage while Janna is out of sight. Janna R Monsoon knocks away an engaging Neeko, so choose your angle carefully while it’s available.

Blitzcrank.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early, and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field deal primarily magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Magic resistance does not block the physical damage from Blitzcrank E Power Fist.
Blitzcrank.combo: Your basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally's crowd control to lock down the enemy and land the ultimate.
Blitzcrank.escape: A missed Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab or depleted mana is your chance to engage. If Blitzcrank E Power Fist and Blitzcrank R Static Field are also down, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom. Blitzcrank has no skill to create distance on his own, so you can force him to use Flash after catching him.
Blitzcrank.fight: Trade right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses or when his mana is depleted. If there's no angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don't force it; whittle him down with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter and wait. Blitzcrank can gain Blitzcrank P Mana Barrier at low health, so secure a way to finish him before attacking.
Blitzcrank.laning: Don't stand side by side with minions; always stand behind them to block Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it easier to hit and extend its root. After Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses, gain an advantage by pushing the lane or trading.
Blitzcrank.phase: In the late game, you have fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: Open the fight from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is locked down by your team's engage. If you use Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone while Blitzcrank still has crowd control, you can be caught while preparing it. Look for an angle to reach enemies behind Blitzcrank, and avoid wasting attacks on him while Blitzcrank P Mana Barrier can activate.
Blitzcrank.watch: Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls in the first target it hits, so dodge it with minions in front of you. If pulled, you can be hit next by the knock-up from Blitzcrank E Power Fist and the silence from Blitzcrank R Static Field. When you don't have vision of a brush, it's hard to know how far his grab can reach, so keep away from brushes.

Anivia.fight: After Anivia Q Flash Frost is used, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and trade with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If Anivia’s revival is still available, don’t try to destroy her egg alone; pressure it with allies.
Anivia.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Anivia’s main damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Anivia.combo: The basic sequence is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then time the landing with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control.
Anivia.escape: When Anivia Q Flash Frost is down, close in on the immobile Anivia and catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If you’re hit by Q, don’t keep fighting; use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s movement speed and brief invisibility to get out of Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Anivia.laning: Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to increase your chance of hitting. If there’s no angle, wait while poking with the third empowered basic attack.
Anivia.phase: In the late game, watch out for Anivia’s terrain control and carefully plan the order in which you use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and R.
Anivia.teamfight: Start fights in the wide lane instead of narrow jungle paths where Anivia W Crystallize can easily block your retreat. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Anivia is caught by an ally’s engage.
Anivia.watch: Anivia Q Flash Frost can detonate mid-flight and stun, so stand outside its range from the start instead of making a slight sidestep based only on its aim. If you’re hit by Q or inside a fully formed Anivia R Glacial Storm, Anivia E Frostbite deals greatly increased damage, so leave the storm immediately.

Akshan.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Akshan is caught by an ally’s engage. If Akshan’s villain mark is on you, don’t face him alone or fight within his execute range. If Akshan R Comeuppance targets a low-health ally, get behind terrain or step in front to block the shots.
Akshan.build: Akshan’s main damage is physical, and Neeko has low armor, so build armor first. Use Cloth Armor to survive early, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots.
Akshan.combo: The basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack.
Akshan.escape: Engage immediately after Akshan E Heroic Swing is down. It’s Akshan’s only mobility tool, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and stop his escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Akshan.fight: The moment after Akshan E Heroic Swing is used is your chance to close the gap. Root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don’t force the trade.
Akshan.laning: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and travels faster when it passes through minions, so cast it at an angle across the wave. Poke Akshan with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Don’t stand only behind minions to dodge Akshan Q Avengerang; watch its return path too.
Akshan.phase: In the late game, carefully plan the order in which you use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Akshan.watch: Akshan Q Avengerang gains range as it hits minions, so dodge both its outgoing and return paths even from behind the wave. Akshan E Heroic Swing uses walls to engage or retreat, so watch his movement near walls. When Akshan R Comeuppance targets you at low health, get behind terrain to block the shots.

Ashe.build: Ashe’s damage is mostly physical, and Neeko has relatively low armor, so build armor first. Start with Cloth Armor to withstand the early game, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots.
Ashe.escape: Ashe has no mobility spell to create distance on her own, so the window after Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is down is a good time to engage. If Ashe W Volley is down and Ashe Q Ranger’s Focus has worn off, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom. Don’t walk in while repeatedly taking hits from Ashe P Frost Shot.
Ashe.fight: Trade after Ashe W Volley is down and Ashe Q Ranger’s Focus has worn off. Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to root Ashe, then follow up with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there’s no opening, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered basic attack and wait.
Ashe.laning: Dodge Ashe W Volley by moving sideways, then look for an opening to land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs right after it’s down. Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows, travels faster, and roots for longer after passing through a minion, so you don’t need to go around the wave. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, avoid forcing a trade and prepare to use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered third basic attack on Ashe.
Ashe.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Ashe is caught by an ally’s engage. Ashe has a hard time escaping on her own once someone gets on top of her, so look for an angle to reach her.
Ashe.watch: Dodge Ashe W Volley’s slowing fan by moving sideways, and look to trade right after it is down. Ashe P Frost Shot’s slow is refreshed with each basic attack, so don’t stay within basic attack range for long. Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow flies in a straight line and stuns, so change direction as you move. While her ultimate is available, don’t start a small skirmish from out of vision.
Ashe.combo: The basic sequence is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s landing hits the target.
Ashe.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.

Aurora.build: Aurora’s main damage is magic, so Neeko should build magic resistance first. Start with Null-Magic Mantle to withstand the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. If Aurora’s healing makes it hard to finish her with one engage, slot Morellonomicon between your core items.
Aurora.combo: Your basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → empowered basic attack. If Aurora uses Aurora W Across the Veil to stealth, aim for where she'll appear instead of casting a skill right away. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then lock down the target with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally's crowd control so the landing hits.
Aurora.escape: If you engage just because Aurora W Across the Veil is down, she can escape with Aurora E The Weirding or Aurora R Between Worlds. Look for the moment when her other mobility skill is also down, especially before Aurora R Between Worlds comes back. Then close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and prevent her escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Aurora.fight: If there's no angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don't force an engage; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's empowered basic attack. If Aurora Q Twofold Hex has hit you and lowered your health, create distance before the return damage increases. Fight by rooting Aurora with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs when she has used one mobility skill to engage and can't escape with another.
Aurora.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow and move faster, extending its root. After it hits, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst to aim for consecutive explosions. If E misses, watch for Aurora to engage. Keep track of Neeko W Shapesplitter's third empowered basic attack so you don't use it on a minion, and land it on Aurora.
Aurora.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using E and R, so carefully plan your engage order for when Aurora's mobility skills are down.
Aurora.teamfight: Neeko starts from the back line with E Tangle-Barbs and finishes with R Pop Blossom after Aurora is locked down by your team's engage. It's a chance to catch Aurora if she used her leap to engage and didn't participate in a takedown, but her leap's cooldown resets when she participates in a takedown, so don't leave low-health allies behind. If Neeko uses R Pop Blossom first and goes in alone, she can be attacked while preparing it or Aurora can escape with a mobility skill.
Aurora.watch: If hit by Aurora Q Twofold Hex, move out of the straight line between Aurora and yourself—the return path—to reduce the second hit's damage. The lower your health, the more damage the return deals, so don't stay while cursed; retreat. When Aurora is stealthed with Aurora W Across the Veil, don't rush Neeko E Tangle-Barbs; aim for where she'll appear. Aurora R Between Worlds slows you when you leave its area, so retreat before it forms or find an angle to fight inside it.

Milio.build: Start by withstanding the early game with Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Milio P Fired Up! and Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick deal magic damage, so magic resistance is the resistance to build first. If Milio’s healing is enough to undo Neeko’s burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Milio.combo: The basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use a basic attack. For an ultimate engage, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land it. Milio R Breath of Life cleanses immobilizing effects but can't remove airborne effects, so use the knock-up from Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Milio.escape: The window to engage opens after Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down. Milio has no mobility, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to make it hard for him to escape.
Milio.fight: When Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down, close the gap, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and deal damage. If you don't have an angle for the root, don't force Neeko E Tangle-Barbs; wait while chipping away at his health with the empowered third attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Milio.laning: Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions so it hits Milio. After landing it, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst across the wave to aim for both poke and wave clear with the chain explosions. Early on, wear down Milio's mana through repeated trades and gain control of the wave.
Milio.phase: Milio's team composition gets stronger over time, so choose the engage order for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom even more carefully in the late game.
Milio.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally's engage. If you press Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught during the preparation.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back the first enemy it hits, so be especially careful when approaching with Neeko R Pop Blossom prepared. When Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and increases the enemy ranged carry's range, delay the frontline fight and let its duration run out.

Morgana.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Morgana’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. If the health Morgana restores with Morgana P Soul Siphon and Morgana W Tormented Shadow is enough to undo Neeko’s burst damage, slot Morellonomicon between your core items.
Morgana.combo: When Morgana E Black Shield is down, root the target with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and a basic attack. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root the target with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land it.
Morgana.escape: Dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding; the window to engage opens when Morgana E Black Shield is down. Morgana has no ability to create distance on her own, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Morgana.fight: Don't waste Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or Neeko R Pop Blossom on a target protected by Morgana E Black Shield. Once the shield is down and you've dodged Morgana Q Dark Binding, close the gap and root the target with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If you don't have an angle, wait while chipping away with the empowered attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Morgana.laning: Stay aligned with the wave so minions block Morgana Q Dark Binding. Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow up with Neeko Q Blooming Burst if it hits. Don't force a fight during the window after you've used Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and missed.
Morgana.phase: In the late game, Neeko has little left to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Morgana.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and check whether Morgana E Black Shield is down. Finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally's engage. If you go in alone with Neeko R Pop Blossom prepared, you can be caught before it lands.
Morgana.watch: Morgana Q Dark Binding only catches the first target it hits, so keep a minion between you and Morgana. If you're caught by Morgana R Soul Shackles, use Neeko R Pop Blossom to get out of range before the stun triggers. When your health is low, don't retreat onto Morgana W Tormented Shadow.

Akali.build: In the early game, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Akali’s damage is mostly magic and Neeko has low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. Akali’s high magic resistance can blunt Neeko’s magic damage, so add some penetration too.
Akali.combo: The basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. Once Akali’s mobility is down, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach for an ultimate, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s landing hits her.
Akali.escape: Don’t go in just because one of Akali W Twilight Shroud, Akali E Shuriken Flip, or Akali R Perfect Execution is down. In particular, before Akali R Perfect Execution is back up, check her remaining mobility tools, then engage with Neeko R Pop Blossom and Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Akali.fight: After dodging the first projectile from Akali E Shuriken Flip, root Akali with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and hit her with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. Fight back when she comes out of Akali W Twilight Shroud to engage, but don’t accept the engage if Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses. Before Akali R Perfect Execution is back up, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and block her escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Akali.laning: Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it easier to hit and extend the root. After it hits, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst to aim for repeated explosions. When there’s no angle, poke with the third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter and save Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Akali.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Akali.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Akali is caught by an ally’s engage or root. You can target Akali with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or Neeko Q Blooming Burst during the brief moment she becomes visible just after entering Akali W Twilight Shroud. If you cast Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught during its windup.
Akali.watch: Dodging the first projectile from Akali E Shuriken Flip is most important. If it marks you, the second dash will follow, so use the movement speed from Neeko W Shapesplitter to dodge the first projectile. You can’t dodge the first dash of Akali R Perfect Execution by walking, so save Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to use against her engage.

Ambessa.build: Use Cloth Armor to survive early, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Ambessa’s damage is mostly physical, and Neeko has low armor, so build armor first. If Ambessa’s healing can undo Neeko’s burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Ambessa.combo: After Ambessa uses her abilities, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with an empowered basic attack. When you have an ultimate angle, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then time the landing with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control. Don’t attack during the windup of Ambessa W Repudiation.
Ambessa.escape: The window to engage is immediately after Ambessa has fully expended all her abilities and all the charges of Ambessa P Drakehound’s Step. While Ambessa E Lacerate is available, watch for its slow followed by Ambessa Q Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam; once it’s down, catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Ambessa.fight: Ambessa can use Ambessa P Drakehound’s Step after each ability to close the gap and land an empowered basic attack, so don’t stand in front of her while her abilities and charges are available. Right after Ambessa uses her abilities and charges, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. Stop attacking during the windup of Ambessa W Repudiation and leave its area.
Ambessa.laning: Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to aim for a root. If there’s no angle, poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter, and watch for Ambessa’s engage after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Ambessa.phase: Both champions grow stronger in the mid game, so wait until Ambessa has used her abilities before fighting. In the late game, Neeko has few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Ambessa.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Ambessa is caught by an ally’s engage. Ambessa R Public Execution can pass through your front line and hit the back line, so don’t stand with Ambessa and your back line in a straight line. If you go in alone while preparing Neeko R Pop Blossom, you can be caught before landing.
Ambessa.watch: When you see the shield and windup from Ambessa W Repudiation, don’t attack; walk out of range. If Ambessa E Lacerate hits you, use Neeko W Shapesplitter to create distance before the slow wears off and dodge the edge of Ambessa Q Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam. Ambessa R Public Execution passes through the ally in front and reaches the farthest champion in a straight line, so don’t stand in that line during a standoff.

Annie.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, then choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Annie’s damage is mostly magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Annie.combo: The basic combo is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root Annie with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s landing hits her.
Annie.escape: The moment Annie uses Annie P Pyromania’s stun is your chance to engage. Annie has no ability to create distance, so close in with Neeko R Pop Blossom and stop her escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Annie.fight: When Annie P Pyromania’s stun is down, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and trade with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there’s no angle to root her, don’t force the cast; wait while poking with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered basic attack.
Annie.laning: Once Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is used, Annie can engage, so cast it when you have a good chance to hit.
Annie.phase: Neeko has very low armor early, so avoid trading while Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready. In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Annie.teamfight: If Annie is missing or Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready, don’t stand clumped with your allies. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Annie is caught by an ally’s engage.
Annie.watch: If white light swirls around Annie, Annie P Pyromania’s stun is ready, so stay out of ability range. After Annie R Summon: Tibbers appears, don’t stay where you are even if you’ve killed Annie; keep your distance from Tibbers.

AurelionSol.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Aurelion Sol's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
AurelionSol.combo: Your basic sequence is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks. If Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land the ultimate.
AurelionSol.escape: Right after you force Aurelion Sol to use Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is your chance to engage. Close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to stop him from escaping. If Aurelion Sol still has crowd control available, he can catch you while you prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, so wait to engage.
AurelionSol.fight: When you see an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, deal damage with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don't force an engage.
AurelionSol.laning: Pressure Aurelion Sol with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs from the start so he can't build up Stardust. It's easier to hit and roots for longer when you throw it through minions. When there's no angle, poke Aurelion Sol with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter, and dodge Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light from behind minions.
AurelionSol.phase: Early, pressure Aurelion Sol with no Stardust using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to slow his growth. In the late game, his permanent Stardust puts you at a disadvantage, so carefully choose your engage order.
AurelionSol.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is locked down by your team's engage. If you use Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught while preparing it. Spread out before engaging so Aurelion Sol R The Skies Descend doesn't hit several of you once he has built up Stardust.
AurelionSol.watch: Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals extra damage and grants Stardust if it hits the same target for a long time, so stand behind minions and quickly move out of its aim. If caught in Aurelion Sol E Singularity, immediately walk out, and when low on health, stay out of its area to avoid being executed. Once he has built up Stardust, spread out from your allies to watch for the knock-up and area shockwave from Aurelion Sol R The Skies Descend.

Azir.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game to withstand Azir's magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for your boots and build magic resistance.
Azir.combo: Your basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land the ultimate.
Azir.escape: Right after you force Azir to use Azir E Shifting Sands is Neeko's chance to engage. Close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, but watch where you'll be pushed if Azir R Emperor's Divide is still available.
Azir.fight: When a soldier is standing still in one place or Azir Q Conquering Sands is down, circle around to approach Azir and take a short trade. Hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there is no angle to root him, poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter and wait.
Azir.laning: When Azir sets up a soldier to farm safely, don't spend a long time trading damage in front of it.
Azir.phase: Neeko has low armor early, so avoid risky trades, but you can pressure Azir with your jungler before he learns his ultimate. Azir grows stronger as the game goes on, so carefully choose the order of your Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom engages in the late game.
Azir.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Azir is locked down by your team's engage. Engage from different directions in open areas so Azir R Emperor's Divide doesn't knock several of you back at once.
Azir.watch: Do not stand in a straight line with Azir W Arise! soldiers. After Azir moves them with Azir Q Conquering Sands, watch out for the slow and follow-up damage. If you enter a narrow passage together, Azir R Emperor's Divide can knock several of you back, so approach from different directions in open areas.

Bard.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Bard P Traveler's Call and Bard Q Cosmic Binding deal magic damage, so build magic resistance. If Bard W Caretaker's Shrine heals enough to offset your burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Bard.combo: Your basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks.
Bard.escape: Right after you force Bard to use Bard E Magical Journey is your window to engage. If Bard Q Cosmic Binding is also down, there's less need to worry about being stunned, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If Bard escapes through a portal, follow him only if it's safe.
Bard.fight: If there's no angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don't force it; poke with the third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Right after Bard uses Bard E Magical Journey, close the gap, root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and deal damage. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don't count on a guaranteed engage; wait for the next chance.
Bard.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst after it hits. If Bard W Caretaker's Shrine is visible in lane, walk over it to remove it.
Bard.phase: In the late game, you have fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Bard.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Bard's side is locked down by your team's engage. Wait for the right moment to deal damage while Bard R Tempered Fate is blocking it.
Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so keep your back away from walls and don't stand in a straight line with allies or minions. Targets caught by Bard R Tempered Fate take no damage, so don't try to deal damage with Neeko Q Blooming Burst during that time.

Brand.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Brand's damage is mostly magic, and Neeko has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Brand.combo: Your basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks.
Brand.escape: The moment Brand uses Brand W Pillar of Flame is your chance to engage. If you're not ablaze, Brand Q Sear can't stun you, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If you're ablaze, dodge Brand Q Sear first, then engage.
Brand.fight: Close the gap after Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and Brand P Blaze isn't applied. Root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If you don't see an angle, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's empowered basic attack and wait.
Brand.laning: If you last-hit next to burning minions, Brand E Conflagration can spread, so step to the side of the wave. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow and move faster, making Brand easier to root. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don't force a trade.
Brand.phase: Early, avoid Brand's Blaze stacks and look for trades only when Neeko E Tangle-Barbs will hit. In the late game, you have fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Brand.teamfight: Spread out from allies before engaging to prevent Brand E Conflagration from spreading and Brand R Pyroclasm from bouncing, and don't stand beside an ally who is ablaze. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then hit Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is locked down by your team's engage. If you press Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be attacked while preparing it.
Brand.watch: If Brand W Pillar of Flame or Brand Q Sear hits first, stacks of Brand P Blaze can build up and trigger an explosion, so dodge his first skill. While ablaze, you can be stunned by Brand Q Sear, so move out of its projectile path or stand behind minions. When Brand R Pyroclasm is cast, spread out from allies to avoid its bounces.

Braum.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Braum's main damage is magic, and Neeko has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Braum P Concussive Blows' stun and the knock-up from Braum R Glacial Fissure are also dangerous, so get tenacity from Mercury's Treads.
Braum.combo: Your basic trade is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks. When engaging after Braum W Stand Behind Me is down, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom. Lock down the enemy with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally's crowd control, then land Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Braum.escape: Braum W Stand Behind Me is his only mobility tool, so the moment he uses it is your chance to close the gap. Approach with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to prevent him from escaping. If marked by Braum P Concussive Blows, first move out of range to avoid the stun from its stacks.
Braum.fight: Start a trade with a root when there's an angle for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to hit. If Braum E Unbreakable is active and blocking from the front, wait for it to end or find an angle from the side his shield isn't facing. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is unavailable, don't force it; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's empowered basic attack and wait for the next chance.
Braum.laning: Braum Q Winter's Bite hits only the first enemy it reaches, so stand behind minions, but avoid a spot where there's a gap between minions and you face Braum in a straight line. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs across the wave so it passes through minions, grows, moves faster, and roots for longer. Poke by hitting Braum with Neeko W Shapesplitter's third empowered basic attack after two basic attacks on minions.
Braum.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Braum.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is locked down by your team's engage. Find an angle that avoids the direction Braum E Unbreakable is facing, and look for a route to reach the target Braum is protecting. Avoid the straight path of Braum R Glacial Fissure, and don't start Neeko R Pop Blossom and go in alone.
Braum.watch: Braum Q Winter's Bite slows and can start stacks of Braum P Concussive Blows, so dodge it from behind minions. If marked, move out of range before the stacks trigger a stun. When Braum R Glacial Fissure is cast, dodge to the side of its straight path and avoid the slow zone left behind.

Cassiopeia.build: Cassiopeia's main damage is magic, and Neeko has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Early, withstand her with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. If Cassiopeia E Twin Fang's healing can offset Neeko's burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Cassiopeia.combo: Your basic sequence is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks. When engaging with Neeko R Pop Blossom, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, then use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally's crowd control to lock down Cassiopeia while preparing your ultimate and land it. Don't start this combo by relying on a mobility skill while standing in Cassiopeia W Miasma.
Cassiopeia.escape: The moment Cassiopeia W Miasma is used elsewhere is your chance to engage. When Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze is cast, first turn your back to avoid the stun, then catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. Cassiopeia has no skill to create distance on her own, so it's important to close the gap and land your root.
Cassiopeia.fight: Avoid extended trades while hit by Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast; after the poison ends, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and attack briefly. Your chance to engage is when Cassiopeia W Miasma has been used elsewhere or after dodging Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze. Once you've closed the gap, catch Cassiopeia, who has no mobility skill, with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Cassiopeia.laning: Hit Cassiopeia with Neeko W Shapesplitter's empowered basic attack, and throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don't force a fight; wait for the next chance.
Cassiopeia.phase: If you don't build a lead early, the mid to late game favors Cassiopeia, so carefully choose your engage order in the late game.
Cassiopeia.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Cassiopeia is locked down by your team's engage. Instead of diving in from the front first, secure vision to cut off Cassiopeia's path or look for the moment Cassiopeia W Miasma is used elsewhere. When engaging, land your root and stun first, then finish the fight before Cassiopeia gains movement speed.
Cassiopeia.watch: If hit by Cassiopeia Q Noxious Blast, Cassiopeia E Twin Fang deals more damage and heals more while you're poisoned, so move out of range and fight again after the poison ends. When you see Cassiopeia R Petrifying Gaze's cast animation, turn your back to avoid being stunned. Don't try to use mobility skills in Cassiopeia W Miasma; walk out instead.

Corki.build: Early on, hold out with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps. Corki’s main damage is mostly physical, so build armor first. True damage from Corki P Hextech Munitions can’t be blocked with resistances, and resistances you build are less effective when you’re hit by Corki E Gatling Gun.
Corki.combo: The basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks. If you use Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Corki can walk out of its area.
Corki.escape: The moment after you make Corki use W Valkyrie is your opening to engage. Close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and stop his escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If Corki W Valkyrie is available, he can cross terrain to escape, so don’t engage first.
Corki.fight: Don’t force a close fight while Corki W Valkyrie is available. Right after he uses Corki W Valkyrie, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there’s no angle for a root, poke and wait with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Corki.laning: Early on, pressure Corki so he can’t farm comfortably, but avoid forced trades given Neeko’s low armor. Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is easier to land and roots for longer when thrown at an angle that passes through minions. Keep your distance after missing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, since Corki can engage.
Corki.phase: Later in the game, Corki has his items and can easily fire missiles from a safe position, so carefully choose your engage order.
Corki.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Corki is caught by your team’s engage. If you use Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be attacked while it prepares. Avoid the front of Corki E Gatling Gun and reposition so you don’t get hit by Corki R Missile Barrage in a row.
Corki.watch: Corki R Missile Barrage also damages targets around the first one it hits, so don’t hide behind minions; get out of range. Reposition in particular so you don’t repeatedly get hit by the third missile. Corki E Gatling Gun shreds armor and magic resistance, so move to the side instead of standing your ground in front of him.

Diana.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Most of Diana’s damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Diana.combo: Root Diana with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks.
Diana.escape: If Diana engages first with E Lunar Rush without a mark from Q Crescent Strike, she has used her mobility. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom, and finish her. If Neeko is hit by Diana Q Crescent Strike, Diana can engage again with E Lunar Rush, so create distance.
Diana.fight: When you can land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, trade with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. Engage after Diana W Pale Cascade’s orbs and shield are gone.
Diana.laning: If you use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, Diana gets an opening to engage, so don’t throw it out carelessly.
Diana.phase: Later in the game, Neeko has little to do after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Diana.teamfight: Use vision to block side-entry routes, and spread out from allies so multiple people aren’t pulled in by Diana R Moonfall. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Diana is caught by your team’s engage. If you press Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught while it prepares.
Diana.watch: Diana Q Crescent Strike curves as it travels, so dodge to the side instead of only backing away. If it hits and marks you, Diana E Lunar Rush resets and she can dive in again, so move away from your current position. Right after Diana W Pale Cascade is activated, don’t stay in close combat until its shield and orbs disappear.

Ekko.build: Most of Ekko’s damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Early on, hold out with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads. If the healing from Ekko R Chronobreak can undo Neeko’s burst damage, fit Morellonomicon in among your core items.
Ekko.combo: The basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack right after Ekko E Phase Dive closes the distance. If you throw Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Ekko can walk out of its area. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the landing hits.
Ekko.escape: Don’t engage just because Ekko E Phase Dive is down. The safest opening is when both the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence and the escape from Ekko R Chronobreak are down. In particular, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs before Ekko R Chronobreak comes back.
Ekko.fight: Without Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, it’s hard to respond to Ekko’s engage, so avoid forced trades. Right after Ekko E Phase Dive closes the distance, he has no mobility available; root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and hit him with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. While Ekko R Chronobreak is down, look for a chance to close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and stop his escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Ekko.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle that passes through minions, and save it if there’s no good angle to land it. In the meantime, basic attack minions twice so your third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter hits Ekko.
Ekko.phase: Later in the game, Neeko has few options left after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order even more carefully.
Ekko.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and if Ekko has just closed the distance with E Phase Dive, use that moment to root him. Finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after your allies’ engage catches the enemy. If Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, you can watch the afterimage’s position and place Neeko Q Blooming Burst where he’ll return.
Ekko.watch: When you see the cast cue for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, avoid the marked area. If you enter it, you can get stunned and give him a shield. Watch which direction Ekko Q Timewinder came from and move out of the return path too. If you see an afterimage behind Ekko, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so don’t chase recklessly even when health is low.

Fizz.build: Most of Fizz’s damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Early on, hold out with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads.
Fizz.combo: The basic order is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. After Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down, when engaging with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom while rooting him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the landing hits. If you throw Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Fizz can walk out of its area.
Fizz.escape: Look to engage right after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down. He can still escape if Fizz Q Urchin Strike is available too, so check whether both mobility abilities have been used, then close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Fizz.fight: Counterattack with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko Q Blooming Burst right after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down. If Fizz Q Urchin Strike is still available, he can escape, so don’t go too deep just because one mobility ability is down. You also have an opening to trade when Fizz W Seastone Trident misses a last hit and goes on its full cooldown.
Fizz.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle that passes through minions to root Fizz, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst after it hits. If there’s no angle for a root, wait while landing an empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter on Fizz. After using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, be ready for Fizz to engage.
Fizz.phase: Later in the game, Neeko has few options left after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Fizz.teamfight: Stand close to your allies and make Fizz use E Playful / Trickster first, then focus him together once it’s down. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after your team’s engage catches the enemy. If the fish from Fizz R Chum the Waters attaches to you, move away from your allies before the shark erupts.
Fizz.watch: Fizz can close the distance with Q Urchin Strike or engage with E Playful / Trickster, so don’t waste Neeko E Tangle-Barbs before he goes in. If the fish from Fizz R Chum the Waters attaches to you, move away from your allies before the shark erupts. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs along Fizz’s approach path as he comes in to follow up on the shark, forcing him to use E Playful / Trickster.

Galio.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Galio’s main magic damage. Choose Mercury’s Treads and prioritize magic resistance.
Galio.combo: Root Galio with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the landing hits.
Galio.escape: Don’t engage just because Galio E Justice Punch is down; look for an opening before Galio R Hero’s Entrance comes back. If Galio W Shield of Durand’s taunt is also down, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and block his escape with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Galio.fight: If there’s no angle to land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don’t force it; poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Galio.laning: Galio is melee and spends a lot of mana, so poke him from range and make him use skills to clear minions. Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and travels faster, and roots for longer, when thrown through minions. Once Galio is low on mana, push the wave to limit his chance to affect other lanes with Galio R Hero’s Entrance.
Galio.phase: Later in the game, Neeko has fewer options after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Galio.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Galio is caught by your team’s engage or uses crowd control. If you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero’s Entrance, leave the area, and while that ability is ready, don’t start a small fight with Galio’s team in another lane.
Galio.watch: When Galio charges W Shield of Durand, he takes reduced damage, so don’t commit your damage; leave the taunt range. Dodge when you see Galio E Justice Punch’s backward movement, and leave the point where both gusts from Galio Q Winds of War overlap. If you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero’s Entrance, leave the area immediately.

Heimerdinger.build: Early on, hold out with Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Most of Heimerdinger’s damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Heimerdinger.combo: The basic combo is to root Heimerdinger with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks.
Heimerdinger.escape: When approaching with Neeko R Pop Blossom, land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Heimerdinger can’t escape.
Heimerdinger.fight: Don’t keep trading head-on in front of his turrets. Approach Heimerdinger himself from the side or through a brush.
Heimerdinger.laning: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and travels faster when thrown at an angle that passes through minions, making it good for rooting Heimerdinger. If there’s no angle, don’t force it; wait while landing the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter on Heimerdinger. Casting Neeko Q Blooming Burst across the wave lets you aim to clear minions and poke at the same time.
Heimerdinger.phase: Neeko has low armor early, so avoid forced trades in front of Heimerdinger’s turret setup. Later in the game, Neeko has few options left after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Heimerdinger is caught by your team’s engage. If Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, don’t group up and face off in one spot around an objective. When entering his turret setup, have a high-health ally hit Heimerdinger first and draw the turrets’ focus.
Heimerdinger.watch: If you’re hit, leave turret range immediately. While Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, watch out for the empowered grenade and rockets, and don’t group up in narrow passages.

Hwei.build: Early on, hold out with Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Most of Hwei’s damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t rely on building only health.
Hwei.combo: The basic order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. To use your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then lock him down with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control so the landing hits.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility ability to create distance on his own, so engage while Hwei E Subject: Torment is down. If you root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs then, Hwei can’t escape. Wait if Hwei E Subject: Torment is available, since you can be rooted or pushed back during your engage.
Hwei.fight: Right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used to poke or clear the wave is your chance to close the distance. Normally, chip away at his health with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter, and start a trade when you have an angle to land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If Hwei’s first ability hits, use the movement speed and brief invisibility from Neeko W Shapesplitter to reposition.
Hwei.laning: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and travels faster, and roots for longer, when thrown at an angle that passes through minions. After it hits, casting Neeko Q Blooming Burst across the wave lets you aim to clear minions and poke at the same time. If there’s no angle for a root, wait while using the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter on Hwei, and play carefully in trades while Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down.
Hwei.phase: Later in the game, Neeko has little to do after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order even more carefully.
Hwei.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Hwei is caught by your team’s engage. Hwei E Subject: Torment being down is your opening to engage; don’t go in first while it’s available. Avoid passages with Hwei’s ground effects and take a wide route to approach.
Hwei.watch: If you’re caught by the root or forced movement from Hwei E Subject: Torment, you can take follow-up damage, so don’t engage first while this ability is available. Hwei completes his damage by hitting you with two different abilities in a row, so if the first hits, reposition immediately to dodge the second. Don’t stay on ground affected by Hwei Q Subject: Disaster either.

Irelia.build: Early on, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps. Irelia’s damage is mostly physical and Neeko has low armor, so build armor first. If Irelia’s healing can undo your burst damage, fit Morellonomicon in among your core items.
Irelia.combo: Root Irelia with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks. When you have an angle to engage while Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the landing hits. When approaching while disguised, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom while Neeko P Inherent Glamour is active.
Irelia.escape: Right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is down is your opening to engage. Check whether Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun is down too, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so she can’t escape.
Irelia.fight: If there’s no good angle, poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter and save Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and trade with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. While Neeko E Tangle-Barbs has missed, watch out for Irelia’s engage.
Irelia.laning: Afterward, don’t leave low-health minions between you and Irelia, and take a step back when minions are about to die. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle that passes through minions, and use the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter on Irelia.
Irelia.phase: Later in the game, Neeko has few options left after using E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so stick to your engage order.
Irelia.teamfight: Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge and Irelia E Flawless Duet have a big impact in team fights, so prioritize targeting Irelia. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Irelia is caught by your team’s engage. If you use Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught during its preparation.
Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can chain in on low-health minions and heal her. Create distance while minions are about to die, and watch out for the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet too. If you’re trapped by Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge, wait until the blades disappear.

Karma.build: Early on, withstand Karma’s damage with a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Karma’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Karma.combo: The basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. If you cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Karma can walk out of its area. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, then prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom and land it by rooting her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Karma.escape: Engage after Karma W Focused Resolve is down to reduce the risk of your engage being interrupted by its tether. After Karma R Mantra empowered Karma E Inspire’s shield expires, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Karma.fight: Dodge Karma Q Inner Flame and chip away at health with the third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Force Karma W Focused Resolve out, then engage after Karma R Mantra empowered Karma E Inspire’s shield expires. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst to deal damage.
Karma.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to improve its hit rate and strengthen its root effect. If there’s no angle, save Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and hit Karma with the third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. If Karma’s spells hit you for free, Karma P Gathering Fire brings Karma R Mantra back sooner, so reposition to dodge them.
Karma.phase: Neeko has very low armor early, so dodge Karma’s poke and wait for an opening to land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. In the late game, Neeko has little to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Karma.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Karma W Focused Resolve is down or your allies have caught the enemy with their engage. Burst damage is ineffective just after Karma R Mantra empowered Karma E Inspire applies its shield, so wait for it to expire. If you press Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, your engage can be interrupted during the preparation.
Karma.watch: Karma R Mantra empowers Karma Q Inner Flame, leaving a patch of fire that explodes again after a short delay. If it hits you, walk out of the circle immediately. Karma W Focused Resolve roots you if the tether stays connected, so create distance as soon as it lands to break the tether. Karma R Mantra empowers Karma W Focused Resolve and heals Karma during the tether, so if you can’t break it, focus your damage before the root lands.

Kassadin.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Kassadin deals mostly magic damage, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Kassadin.combo: The basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. Use it when Kassadin Q Null Sphere is down to reduce the magic damage absorbed by its shield. When you have an opening to engage while Kassadin R Riftwalk is down, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Kassadin.escape: During a chase, if Kassadin runs out of mana, he can’t cast R Riftwalk again, so counterattack then.
Kassadin.fight: When you have an angle to hit with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, throw it through minions to root Kassadin, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst.
Kassadin.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow larger, travel faster, and root for longer. Avoid unnecessary spell casts when Kassadin is close, and clear the wave outside Kassadin’s range whenever possible.
Kassadin.phase: In the late game, Kassadin can use Kassadin R Riftwalk to get into the back line and escape, so don’t stand alone within its range.
Kassadin.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Kassadin is caught by an ally’s engage. While transformed, Neeko R Pop Blossom’s windup is hidden, so use the angle created by transforming to approach. Kassadin can use Kassadin R Riftwalk to get into the back line, so don’t stand alone and look for a chance to catch him with an immobilizing effect.
Kassadin.watch: Kassadin Q Null Sphere’s shield absorbs Neeko’s magic poke, so deal damage after Kassadin Q Null Sphere is down. Kassadin E Force Pulse slows you and comes back sooner as nearby spells are cast, so avoid unnecessary spell casts.

Leblanc.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand LeBlanc’s magic damage early. Choose Mercury’s Treads and prioritize magic resistance. Neeko’s main magic damage is effective against LeBlanc’s low magic resistance.
Leblanc.combo: The basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. This combo is hard to escape after LeBlanc W Distortion’s return expires or has been used. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land the ultimate.
Leblanc.escape: Right after you make LeBlanc use LeBlanc W Distortion is your chance to close the distance. Approach with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, but watch whether she returns while she still can. If LeBlanc E Ethereal Chains hits you, leave its range before the root lands; you can use Neeko R Pop Blossom as a movement tool.
Leblanc.fight: Don’t force Neeko E Tangle-Barbs while LeBlanc W Distortion is available. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and deal damage after she uses LeBlanc W Distortion to engage or her chance to return has passed. If there’s no opening, wait while poking with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Leblanc.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it easier to hit and extend the root. Cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst across the wave to aim for minion kills and poke at the same time. If LeBlanc pushes the lane and disappears from vision, alert your team immediately.
Leblanc.phase: In the late game, Neeko has little to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Leblanc.teamfight: Start the fight from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after LeBlanc W Distortion is down or your allies have caught the enemy with their engage. Approach while transformed with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to hide Neeko R Pop Blossom’s windup. If you cast Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught during the windup, so coordinate with your allies’ engage.
Leblanc.watch: If LeBlanc Q Sigil of Malice’s mark is still on you, her next spell deals more damage, so don’t step forward; back away and give the mark time to disappear. LeBlanc E Ethereal Chains doesn’t root you immediately on hit, so leave its range while the tether remains connected. If LeBlanc P Mirror Image makes her appear as two, don’t rush your spells; identify which one is real by watching which one attacks.

Leona.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to build magic resistance. Choose Mercury’s Treads.
Leona.combo: When Leona E Zenith Blade is down, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and a basic attack. If you cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Leona can walk out of its area. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land the ultimate.
Leona.escape: Right after you make her use that ability, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so she can’t escape. If Leona Q Shield of Daybreak or Leona R Solar Flare’s crowd control is still available, don’t engage first with Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Leona.fight: Right after Leona E Zenith Blade is down is your chance to close the distance. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then counterattack with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. Don’t force trades while Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is unavailable.
Leona.laning: Avoid melee trades early, considering Leona’s high armor and Neeko’s low armor. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to aim for a root. If there’s no angle, wait while poking Leona with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Leona.phase: Early on, Leona’s high armor and Neeko’s low armor make it hard for Neeko to absorb her engage. In the late game, Neeko has few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Leona.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, absorb Leona’s engage, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after your allies catch the enemy. If Leona P Sunlight marks you, that signals follow-up damage is coming, so back away immediately. Use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s brief invisibility and clone to disrupt Leona E Zenith Blade’s aim.
Leona.watch: Leona E Zenith Blade pierces in a straight line and attaches Leona to the last champion hit, so don’t stand in a line with an ally. Leona can activate Leona Q Shield of Daybreak before approaching, so watch your distance rather than whether she has used the spell. When Leona W Eclipse is active, leave its area before it explodes. When Leona R Solar Flare’s indicator appears, move sideways to avoid the center stun.

Lissandra.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Lissandra’s main damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If Lissandra R Frozen Tomb’s self-targeted healing interferes with finishing her, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Lissandra.combo: The basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. While Lissandra E Glacial Path’s claw is traveling, you can use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to stop Lissandra from recasting the ability. Once Lissandra’s escape is down and you have an angle to root her, approach while transformed, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land the ultimate.
Lissandra.escape: Right after Lissandra E Glacial Path has been used is your window to close the distance. Approach with Neeko R Pop Blossom and hit her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so she can’t escape. At low levels, use the moment just after Lissandra W Ring of Frost is also down to trade.
Lissandra.fight: Trade right after Lissandra W Ring of Frost is used on the wave or misses. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there’s no angle for a root, wait while poking with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. If Lissandra R Frozen Tomb is available, don’t put all your damage in at once; spread it out until the self-targeted stasis ends.
Lissandra.laning: Stand at an angle to allied minions to avoid Lissandra Q Ice Shard’s piercing path. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to root Lissandra, then cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst across the wave to poke and clear the lane together. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, stop forcing trades and watch for Lissandra’s engage.
Lissandra.phase: In the late game, Neeko has few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so carefully choose your engage order.
Lissandra.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Lissandra E Glacial Path is down or your allies have caught the enemy with their engage. Approaching while transformed can hide Neeko R Pop Blossom’s windup, but chain it with a root so the enemy can’t spread out during the windup. If Lissandra R Frozen Tomb is available, spread out your finishing damage until her self-targeted stasis ends.
Lissandra.watch: Lissandra Q Ice Shard pierces after hitting a minion, so don’t stand in a line with allied minions. If Lissandra W Ring of Frost roots you or Lissandra R Frozen Tomb stuns you, you can take a string of damage, so don’t force an approach while both spells are available.

Lux.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Lux’s main damage is magic, so Neeko should build magic resistance first.
Lux.combo: The basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with a basic attack. When Lux Q Light Binding misses and you engage, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour to approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Lux.escape: The moment Lux Q Light Binding misses is your chance to engage. Lux has no spell to create distance on her own, so close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
