Lux.fight: Bait Lux Q Light Binding and dodge it, then close the distance from a brush or the side. Lux has no mobility spell, so root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks.
Lux.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to extend the root, then place Neeko Q Blooming Burst after it hits. When there’s no angle for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don’t force it; poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Lux Q Light Binding can pierce the first target, so don’t stand in a line with an ally.
Lux.phase: Neeko has low armor early, so trade carefully while waiting for an angle to land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. In the late game, Neeko has little to do after using E and R, so plan your engage order even more carefully.
Lux.teamfight: Approach from different directions, spread out from your allies so Lux E Lucent Singularity doesn’t catch you all together. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Lux is caught by an ally’s engage.
Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits you, you’re likely to get hit by her follow-up spells too, so dodge sideways when Lux casts it and don’t stand in a line with an ally. Leave the area where Lux E Lucent Singularity lands, and move sideways when you see the red targeting line for Lux R Final Spark. If Lux’s spells hit you, create distance so you don’t also get hit by a basic attack that triggers Lux P Illumination.

Malzahar.build: Start with a Null-Magic Mantle in the early game to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Malzahar's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. To counter Malzahar R Nether Grasp, buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar to cleanse the suppression.
Malzahar.combo: First break Malzahar P Void Shift with Neeko Q Blooming Burst or another ability, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs cast through minions.
Malzahar.escape: Malzahar has no mobility to create distance, so dodge Malzahar Q Call of the Void and break Malzahar P Void Shift before looking for an engage. If the Voidlings summoned by Malzahar W Void Swarm are already on the field, clear them first with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. If Malzahar can cast Malzahar R Nether Grasp, don't engage alone; fight where an ally can interrupt the cast.
Malzahar.fight: When Malzahar P Void Shift is active, it blocks Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so remove Void Shift first with Neeko Q Blooming Burst or another ability. If you don't have an angle for E, poke with the empowered attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter while you wait. Dodge Malzahar Q Call of the Void, then root him with E and deal damage once Void Shift has been removed.
Malzahar.laning: When Malzahar casts Malzahar E Malefic Visions on the wave, take a step back from the infected minion to avoid the effect jumping to you. Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to aim for a longer root. If Malzahar is pushing the lane, work with your jungler to remove Void Shift and create a chance to take him down.
Malzahar.phase: Early on, push or pressure the lane so Malzahar has no chance to build up, and avoid risky fights when Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is unavailable. Neeko peaks in mid game as her ability power builds, so create opportunities with a root and ultimate after removing Void Shift. Malzahar gets stronger over time, making the matchup harder, so carefully choose the engage order for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom in the late game.
Malzahar.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally's engage. If an ally is caught by Malzahar R Nether Grasp, apply immobilizing crowd control to Malzahar to interrupt the cast.
Malzahar.watch: When a minion afflicted by Malzahar E Malefic Visions dies, the effect jumps to the nearest enemy, so move away from that minion. When you see Malzahar Q Call of the Void, move outside the two portals and don't engage until the silence ends. Malzahar R Nether Grasp can't be cleansed with Neeko W Shapesplitter, so don't walk alone through an area without vision while Malzahar can use his ultimate.

Maokai.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Maokai deals mostly magic damage and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the healing from Maokai P Sap Magic is enough to offset your burst damage, buy Morellonomicon between your core items.
Maokai.combo: For trades, root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. Don't use basic attacks during Maokai W Twisted Advance's dash; attack after he lands.
Maokai.escape: The window to engage opens immediately after you make Maokai use Maokai W Twisted Advance. Disrupt his aim with the brief invisibility and clone from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Once you confirm Maokai W Twisted Advance is down, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp is still available, also check that you have room to dodge its root.
Maokai.fight: Keep your distance while Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready, then move forward to trade right after he uses it. Root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and land Neeko Q Blooming Burst. In general, avoid repeatedly hitting Maokai with abilities, which can trigger Maokai P Sap Magic's healing sooner.
Maokai.laning: Early on, it's hard to withstand an engage from Maokai W Twisted Advance, so don't overextend near bushes. Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, and save it if you don't have an angle. While you wait, poke Maokai with the empowered third attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Maokai.phase: In the late game, Neeko has little left to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Maokai.teamfight: Fight in open terrain while avoiding the path of Maokai R Nature's Grasp. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then hit the enemy with Neeko R Pop Blossom after they are caught by an ally's engage. It's better to use abilities on the enemy carry than on Maokai, since they can trigger his healing sooner.
Maokai.watch: Maokai W Twisted Advance is dangerous because it roots and dashes, so don't enter range near bushes while it's ready. Avoid bushes with Maokai E Sapling Toss, and if a sapling chases you, lead it toward a minion or monster rather than an ally. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp comes from a distance, dodge perpendicular to its direction of travel.

Mel.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Mel's main damage is magic and Neeko has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Mel.combo: Bait out Mel W Rebuttal first, then use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. After rooting with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst so it's easier to land the follow-up explosions. For an ultimate engage, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach → prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom → root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → land Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Mel.escape: The window for Neeko to engage opens after Mel E Solar Snare is down. If Mel W Rebuttal is down too, you can try Neeko E Tangle-Barbs without worrying about it being reflected.
Mel.fight: Poke with the empowered attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter, then start a fight with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs once Mel W Rebuttal is down. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don't force Neeko Q Blooming Burst; wait for another opening.
Mel.laning: Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to root Mel. If Neeko Q Blooming Burst hits both the wave and Mel, you can clear the wave while poking her. Push and pressure the lane early before Mel's scaling through Mel R Golden Eclipse builds up.
Mel.phase: Push and pressure the lane early to slow Mel's scaling. In the late game, Mel's accumulated scaling becomes a threat, and Neeko runs out of steam after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Mel.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, but watch out for Mel W Rebuttal if it's still available. After an ally's engage or a root catches the enemy, go in with Neeko R Pop Blossom to land an AoE stun. If you prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be caught before it lands, so wait for the right moment.
Mel.watch: Mel W Rebuttal reflects projectiles, so bait it out with a basic attack before casting Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. Mel E Solar Snare roots you if you're hit by its center, so sidestep it; if you're hit, watch out for the follow-up Mel Q Radiant Volley. If repeated hits build up Overwhelm, retreat even if you still have health, and after a fight watch for Mel R Golden Eclipse until the stacks disappear.

Nami.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Nami deals mostly magic damage and Neeko has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the healing from Nami W Ebb and Flow is enough to offset your burst damage, buy Morellonomicon between your core items.
Nami.combo: The basic order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. To engage with Neeko R Pop Blossom, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, then prepare R and catch Nami with E or an ally's crowd control so Pop Blossom lands.
Nami.escape: The window to engage opens right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Dodge Nami R Tidal Wave by walking to the side, and save Neeko W Shapesplitter for the follow-up Q. Nami has no mobility, so close the gap and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to prevent her from escaping.
Nami.fight: Close the gap on Nami right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and a basic attack. If you don't have an angle for E, don't force it; chip away at her health with the empowered third attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Nami.laning: Nami has low health and no mobility, so secure vision and look for an angle on her rather than the ranged carry. Cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to aim for a hit, then follow up with Neeko Q Blooming Burst if it hits. Once E is spent, the enemy can engage, so wait for another opening.
Nami.phase: In the late game, you have few tools left after using E and R, so choose your engage order more carefully.
Nami.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Nami or another enemy is caught by an ally's engage. If Nami Q Aqua Prison and Nami R Tidal Wave crowd control are still available, going in alone while preparing R first can get you caught before it lands.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison stuns you if it hits, so walk sideways to dodge when you see its indicator appear. When you see Nami R Tidal Wave, also move to the side; save Neeko W Shapesplitter to dodge the follow-up Q. Don't fight head-on against an enemy empowered by Nami E Tidecaller's Blessing; re-engage after its duration ends.

Nautilus.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Nautilus's main damage is magic and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Nautilus.combo: The basic order is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and a basic attack. Landing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions gives it a longer root, making it easier to land the chain explosions from Neeko Q Blooming Burst. To engage with your ultimate, transform with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root the enemy with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land it.
Nautilus.escape: The window to engage opens right after you make Nautilus use Nautilus Q Dredge Line. When Nautilus's only engage is down, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. After the fight, use the brief invisibility and clone from Neeko W Shapesplitter to disrupt the direction of pursuit as you retreat.
Nautilus.fight: Trade right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses. Root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and a basic attack before moving out of Nautilus P Staggering Blow's attack range. Don't accept an engage when Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is unavailable.
Nautilus.laning: Stand behind minions to block Nautilus Q Dredge Line, and cast Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions. If you don't have an angle for the root, wait while using the empowered attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter on the enemy. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, Nautilus has an opening to engage, so keep your distance.
Nautilus.phase: In the late game, Neeko has few tools left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Nautilus.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally's engage. Nautilus R Depth Charge follows its target and knocks up allies along its path, so don't stand on top of an ally while Nautilus has his ultimate. If Nautilus still has strong crowd control available, don't press Neeko R Pop Blossom and go in alone.
Nautilus.watch: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is his only engage and a major kill threat, so use minions to block it. Nautilus P Staggering Blow roots you with his first basic attack, so stay outside his attack range. If Nautilus E Riptide hits you at close range, move before the waves end to avoid the following explosion.

Orianna.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Orianna’s magic damage early. Choose Mercury’s Treads and prioritize magic resistance.
Orianna.combo: The standard order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → empowered basic attack. Use Q after rooting so Orianna is more likely to remain in its blast radius. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with E so R hits when you land.
Orianna.escape: Orianna has no ability to create distance on her own, so the moment after the orb moves away from her is your chance to close in. Avoid the area around the orb where Orianna R Command: Shockwave can reach you. If the slow from Orianna W Command: Dissonance and R’s forced movement are down, close in with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with E Tangle-Barbs.
Orianna.fight: Look for a trade right after Orianna uses Q Command: Attack to send the orb away from herself. Her E Command: Protect’s sustained defensive stats are unavailable then, so land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. Don’t take extended fights where Orianna’s P Clockwork Windup makes her consecutive basic attacks stronger.
Orianna.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to strengthen the root and make it easier to hit Orianna. When you don’t have an angle, save E and harass by tracking the empowered basic attack cycle from Neeko W Shapesplitter. After using E, Neeko has a harder time landing a guaranteed follow-up, so back off while watching the orb’s position.
Orianna.phase: In the late game, Neeko loses much of her threat after using E Tangle-Barbs and R, so choose your engage order carefully.
Orianna.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after enemies, including Orianna, are caught by your team’s engage. The area around Orianna’s orb is dangerous because of Orianna R Command: Shockwave, so approach from elsewhere. Disguise to hide R’s windup, but don’t enter the enemy team alone while preparing it.
Orianna.watch: Watch where Orianna Q Command: Attack places the orb and position accordingly. Near the orb, Orianna R Command: Shockwave can pull you in, so don’t approach while watching only Orianna herself. Watch out for the slow from Orianna W Command: Dissonance, too.

Pantheon.build: Early on, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps. Pantheon’s main damage is physical and Neeko’s armor is low, so prioritize armor. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid choices that only greatly increase your health.
Pantheon.combo: Root Pantheon with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with basic attacks. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault is blocking damage from the front, wait for it to end or angle in from the side.
Pantheon.escape: Your chance to engage is after Pantheon W Shield Vault is down and before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back. Close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so he can’t get away. If only one of Pantheon’s mobility abilities is down, he can escape with the other, so don’t rush your engage.
Pantheon.fight: Early on, stay out of Pantheon W Shield Vault range and harass with the empowered third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault ends or you get an angle from the side, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and hit Neeko Q Blooming Burst. If Pantheon still has a mobility ability available, don’t rush in with Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Pantheon.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the damage from Pantheon Q Comet Spear. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it larger and faster and increase the root duration. After Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, watch out for Pantheon's engage and keep your distance.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon has less influence in the late game, but Neeko also has few options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so stick to your engage order.
Pantheon.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by your team’s engage. Approaching while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour can hide Neeko R Pop Blossom’s windup, but if you go in alone while preparing it, the enemy may scatter. If you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, move outside its landing area.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault targets and stuns you, so create distance before you enter its range. While Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, it blocks damage from the front; wait for it to end or attack from the side. If you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, move outside its landing area.

Pyke.build: Early on, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps. Pyke’s damage is mostly physical, so prioritize armor, but also get health to stay above his execute threshold since he stacks armor penetration. If Pyke’s healing is enough to undo your burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Pyke.combo: Root Pyke with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If you cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Pyke can walk out of its area. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the ultimate hits when you land.
Pyke.escape: The moment after dodging Pyke E Phantom Undertow is your chance to engage, but check whether Pyke R Death From Below is still available. Before Pyke R Death From Below comes back, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to prevent his escape.
Pyke.fight: If you don’t have an angle to land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don’t force it; harass with empowered basic attacks from Neeko W Shapesplitter. After dodging Pyke E Phantom Undertow to the side, Pyke has difficulty engaging or escaping, so root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and fight. If Pyke R Death From Below is also down, that’s your chance to close in with Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Pyke.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to create a root angle. Don’t use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered basic attack on minions; hit Pyke with it. If Pyke backs off after a trade, maintain vision or ward that area to prevent healing from Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones.
Pyke.phase: In the late game, there's a long downtime after Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Pyke.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Pyke is caught by your team’s engage. Don’t stand next to low-health allies, so you aren’t caught in Pyke R Death From Below with them. If you see the shark shadow from Pyke W Ghostwater Dive or Pyke E Phantom Undertow is still available, first move to a safe position.
Pyke.watch: If you see the shark shadow beneath you while Pyke W Ghostwater Dive is active, you’re already in range, so move back toward an ally or turret. Pyke E Phantom Undertow leaves a stun along his dash path, so sidestep to the side of the direction he came from. Watch out for Pyke R Death From Below when your health is low.

Qiyana.build: Buy Cloth Armor early and choose Plated Steelcaps. Qiyana P Royal Privilege, Q Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal, and E Audacity deal mostly physical damage, so prioritize armor. Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent deals damage based on maximum health, so be careful about choices that only greatly increase your health.
Qiyana.combo: In lane, land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst and follow with a basic attack. If you use Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Qiyana can walk out of its area. To engage with your ultimate after Qiyana’s mobility is down, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the ultimate hits when you land.
Qiyana.escape: The moment after Qiyana uses both W Terrashape and E Audacity is Neeko’s chance to engage. In particular, before Qiyana E Audacity comes back, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so she can’t escape. If Qiyana is holding the river element, wait for an opening from outside the root range of Qiyana Q Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal.
Qiyana.fight: Counterattack after both Qiyana W Terrashape and Qiyana E Audacity are down, especially before Qiyana E Audacity comes back. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If only one is down, she can escape with the other mobility ability, so don’t rush your engage.
Qiyana.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions; if you don’t have an angle, save it and harass with the empowered third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Watch out for Qiyana’s engage right after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Qiyana.phase: In the late game, build armor and move with your team. Choose your engage order carefully after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Qiyana.teamfight: Move with your team away from terrain to limit Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent’s angles. Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Qiyana is caught by your team’s engage or has used a mobility ability. If you prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom first and enter alone, Qiyana may catch you before it lands.
Qiyana.watch: If Qiyana approaches holding the river element, first move out of range of the root from Qiyana Q Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal. If she disappears with the brush element, move into allied vision. When you’re below half health, keep your distance from Qiyana holding the rock element. Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent explodes on contact with terrain, so don’t stand with your back to a wall and avoid riverbanks and narrow passages.

Rakan.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first, and choose Mercury’s Treads. Rakan’s main damage is magic and Neeko’s magic resistance is relatively low, so prioritize magic resistance.
Rakan.combo: The standard order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. Watch Rakan W Grand Entrance’s landing point and hit him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to keep him in Neeko Q Blooming Burst’s area. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then time the landing with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control.
Rakan.escape: The moment after you make Rakan use W Grand Entrance is Neeko’s window to close the gap. If Rakan is moving alone and separated from allied champions, he can’t escape with Rakan E Battle Dance, so look for a chance to catch him. If you close in with Neeko R Pop Blossom, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so he can’t get away.
Rakan.fight: Look to trade right after the shield from Rakan P Fey Feathers is removed. If Rakan W Grand Entrance is down, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks.
Rakan.laning: Early on, it’s difficult to respond to Rakan W Grand Entrance, so watch its landing point and sidestep. Aim Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions; when you don’t have an angle, wait and harass with the empowered third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. After missing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, watch out for Rakan’s engage.
Rakan.phase: In the late game, Neeko has fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Rakan.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and if Rakan engages with W Grand Entrance, aim for his visible landing point and root him. Finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after your team’s engage catches the enemy. When Rakan R The Quickness is active, don’t line up with allies, and use crowd control before he reaches you.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance’s landing point is visible in advance, so sidestep when the dash starts to avoid the knock-up. When Rakan R The Quickness is active, it’s hard to escape on foot; don’t line up with allies, and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or put terrain between you before he reaches you.

Rell.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Rell’s damage is mostly magic and Neeko’s magic resistance is low, so prioritize magic resistance.
Rell.combo: The standard order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attack. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the ultimate hits when you land.
Rell.escape: If only Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down is down, she can escape with Rell E Full Tilt, so wait to engage. Once both mobility abilities are down, especially before E comes back, you have a chance to approach with Neeko R Pop Blossom and land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Rell.fight: Harass from outside Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down range, then create distance right after she uses W. After Rell E Full Tilt is also down, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so she can’t escape.
Rell.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to root Rell, then cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst. When you don’t have a root angle, save E and harass with the empowered third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Rell has low magic resistance early and no way to restore health, so keep chipping away at her from outside her engage range.
Rell.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using E and R, so choose your engage order more carefully.
Rell.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. After avoiding Rell’s engage and the enemy is caught by your team’s engage, finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom. Keep your distance from allies so several of you aren’t pulled in by Rell R Magnet Storm.
Rell.watch: If Rell and an ally both speed up from Rell E Full Tilt, that’s a signal she’s about to engage. Stop trading and move outside Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down range. Before a team fight, spread out from your allies so several of you aren’t pulled in by Rell R Magnet Storm.

Renata.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Renata Glasc’s damage is mostly magic, so Neeko should prioritize magic resistance. If the healing from Renata Glasc W Bailout is enough to undo burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Renata.combo: The standard combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then follow with basic attacks. If you can get close to Renata Glasc, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the ultimate hits when you land. If you cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst first, Renata Glasc can walk out of its area.
Renata.escape: Renata Glasc has no mobility ability of her own, so close the gap during the window after Renata Glasc Q Handshake’s root is down. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is still available, engage while keeping your distance from allies, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and hit her with Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Renata.fight: When you can land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, trade with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If you don’t have an angle, don’t force Neeko E Tangle-Barbs; chip away at her with empowered basic attacks from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Renata Glasc has no mobility ability of her own, so closing in and rooting her can create a chance to catch her.
Renata.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to look for an angle to hit Renata Glasc. Count your basic attacks ahead so the empowered third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter hits Renata Glasc. Sidestep Renata Glasc E Loyalty Program, and if Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down, don’t force a play until the next opening.
Renata.phase: In the late game, Neeko has few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Renata.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Renata Glasc is caught by your team’s engage. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is still available, keep your distance from allies so you aren’t hit together.
Renata.watch: Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots the first target it hits and can throw them to stun an ally, so dodge it by standing behind minions or your frontline. If you're hit by Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover, you'll attack nearby allies, so keep your distance from them while this ability is available. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, back off rather than chasing the revived enemy, to prevent an ally from dying.

Ryze.build: Ryze's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. Build Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Ryze.combo: The basic order is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. After rooting Ryze, cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst so its re-explosion hits too. To engage with your ultimate, approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then immobilize Ryze with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or allied crowd control so Pop Blossom hits when you land.
Ryze.escape: If Ryze has used Ryze W Rune Prison too, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Ryze.fight: After dodging Ryze E Spell Flux, start a trade by landing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs beyond minions. If there is no angle, poke and wait with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Do not force an engage after missing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Ryze.laning: Before his items come online, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so pressure his scaling from early on. Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and travels faster when sent through minions, so look for an angle through the wave. Hitting both the wave and Ryze with Neeko Q Blooming Burst lets you clear the wave and poke at the same time.
Ryze.phase: In the late game, you lose power after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Ryze.teamfight: Start the fight from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then engage with Neeko R Pop Blossom when Ryze is caught up in an allied engage. If you let Ryze stay within range and keep hitting you, the mark is refreshed, so interrupt his combo when you land crowd control. If you are marked by Ryze E Spell Flux, move away from allies to prevent the damage from bouncing to nearby targets.
Ryze.watch: If Ryze E Spell Flux hits you, move away from allies until the mark disappears. While marked, Ryze W Rune Prison roots you, and Ryze Q Overload is empowered and bounces to nearby targets. If you see Ryze R Realm Warp, watch the arrival point; if you can reach Ryze, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to cancel it.

Senna.build: Senna's main damage is physical, and Neeko has low armor, so build Cloth Armor early to survive. Choose Plated Steelcaps for boots, and build armor along with health instead of stacking health alone. If the healing from Senna Q Piercing Darkness can undo Neeko's burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between core items.
Senna.combo: The basic order is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. If you cast Q first, Senna can walk out of its area. To engage, approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root with E to land as you come down.
Senna.escape: Look for an engage angle when Senna W Last Embrace misses or is down. Senna has no skill to create distance herself, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to make it hard for her to escape.
Senna.fight: Find an angle to send Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow a hit with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there is no angle for a root, do not force E; poke with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. After Senna W Last Embrace is down, close the gap and look for a chance to land the root.
Senna.laning: When a soul appears, Senna has to step forward, so watch that spot in advance and poke with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko Q Blooming Burst. E grows and travels faster when sent through minions, so look for an angle through the wave instead of going around it. Since Neeko has low armor early, avoid trades where Senna hits you twice in a row while you prevent her from collecting mist.
Senna.phase: Early on, Senna's low health lets you strongly disrupt her soul collection, but Neeko also has low armor, so focus trades on landing E. In the late game, Senna's range and Attack Damage grow, so Neeko must plan the order of her E and R engages more carefully.
Senna.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Senna and the enemy are caught up in an allied engage. If you see Senna E Curse of the Black Mist, retreat to a spot with vision or use an area ability like Neeko Q Blooming Burst to prevent an engage through the mist. If you press R first and go in alone, you can be caught while preparing, so time it with a root or allied crowd control.
Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness travels in a straight line through minions or allies, so move out of the line connecting Senna to her target. Dodge Senna W Last Embrace from behind minions, and if you are marked, move away from allies before the root spreads. If Senna hits you once, retreat immediately so you do not give her mist with a second attack.

Seraphine.build: Build Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Seraphine's damage is mostly magic, and Neeko has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the healing from Seraphine W Surround Sound can undo your burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between core items.
Seraphine.combo: The basic combo is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. After Seraphine E Beat Drop is down, if you approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land as you come down.
Seraphine.escape: The moment after Seraphine E Beat Drop is down is your window to engage. Seraphine has no mobility, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to make it hard for her to escape.
Seraphine.fight: Trade when Seraphine is standing alone away from her ADC or just after she uses Seraphine E Beat Drop. Root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. Close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom when you engage.
Seraphine.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow and travel faster, making it easier to hit Seraphine. If there is no angle, do not force it; wait while hitting Seraphine with the third empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. After using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, watch your distance so Seraphine does not get an opening.
Seraphine.phase: Build magic resistance early and wait for an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order more carefully.
Seraphine.teamfight: Spread out to the sides from your allies so Seraphine R Encore cannot chain through multiple people. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom when Seraphine is caught up in an allied engage or after Seraphine E Beat Drop is down.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots slowed enemies and stuns immobilized enemies. If you are slowed, move out of the direct line in front of you. In teamfights, spread out to the sides so Seraphine R Encore's charm cannot pass through an ally and reach the back line.

Sona.build: Sona’s damage is mostly magic, so withstand it early with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads. If the healing from Sona W Aria of Perseverance is enough to undo burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between your core items.
Sona.combo: Root Sona with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, then follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, approach while disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to time the landing.
Sona.escape: If Sona R Crescendo is available, she can stun you during your engage, so look for an opening after she uses it. Engage before Sona increases her movement speed with E Song of Celerity, and catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Sona.fight: When Sona moves forward to apply an aura, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and deal damage. Sona can speed herself up with E Song of Celerity, so land your root first instead of relying on a slow to chase her.
Sona.laning: Trade consistently while Sona is weak early to make her spend mana on healing. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions; if you don’t have an angle, wait and harass with empowered basic attacks from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Sona.phase: Sona is weak early, so Neeko should keep her pressured with trades.
Sona.teamfight: Spread out from your allies to the sides to avoid Sona R Crescendo’s linear stun. Start with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Sona is caught by your team’s engage. If you separate Sona from her group, her healing, shields, and movement speed auras can’t reach her allies.
Sona.watch: Sona R Crescendo stuns enemies in a line, so don’t stand in a line with your allies when Sona moves forward. When she approaches to land an empowered basic attack, watch out for the bonus damage or slow from Sona P Power Chord and create distance.

Soraka.build: Build Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Soraka Q Starcall and E Equinox deal magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If Soraka's healing can withstand Neeko's burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between core items.
Soraka.combo: The basic order is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to land as you come down.
Soraka.escape: Your chance to engage comes just after Soraka uses Soraka E Equinox for poke or wave clear. Soraka has no mobility to create distance, so close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Soraka.fight: Engage once you see Soraka E Equinox is down. Root Soraka with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If there is no angle for a root, poke and wait with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Soraka.laning: Pressure the enemy ADC to make Soraka use Soraka W Astral Infusion, which costs Soraka health. To keep up this pressure, avoid Soraka Q Starcall. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it easier to hit and extend the root.
Soraka.phase: Build resistance early against Soraka's magic damage, and wait for an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Soraka.teamfight: Focus Soraka herself rather than continually attacking an ally she is healing. Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then engage with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Soraka E Equinox is down or the enemy is caught up in an allied engage. Concentrate your damage in a short time before Soraka R Wish heals them.
Soraka.watch: Entering Soraka E Equinox's zone silences you and can also root you, so use your engage ability before stepping into it. Avoid Soraka Q Starcall, which slows Neeko and grants Soraka healing and movement speed.

Swain.build: Swain's main damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Build Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If Swain's healing can undo Neeko's burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between core items.
Swain.combo: The basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. When Swain E Nevermove is down, approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then hold the enemy in place with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or allied crowd control so the landing hits. You can use Neeko R Pop Blossom while disguised, and the disguise ends shortly afterward, so choose carefully where you begin preparing.
Swain.escape: Swain has no mobility or escape, so the moment after Swain E Nevermove is down is your window to engage. Close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so he cannot escape. If Swain E Nevermove is returning, delay your engage until the wave disappears completely.
Swain.fight: The moment after Swain E Nevermove is completely down is your chance to fight. Until then, keep your distance, poke with the empowered third basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter, and wait for an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Swain.laning: Take lane control early before Swain builds up his scaling stacks. Last-hit near maximum range to avoid being hit by multiple bolts from Swain Q Death's Hand, and dodge the return path of Swain E Nevermove too. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to improve your chance to hit; if it misses, do not force an engage.
Swain.phase: Swain has few scaling stacks early, so Neeko should take lane control and keep him pressured. In the late game, Swain's permanent scaling and healing make the matchup increasingly unfavorable, so build Grievous Wounds and plan your engage order carefully.
Swain.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Swain is caught up in an allied engage. If Swain R Demonic Ascension is active, do not fight beside him for long; move out of its area and wait for it to end. When you go back in, account for Swain's healing by applying Grievous Wounds.
Swain.watch: Swain E Nevermove travels out and then returns, so after dodging the first wave, stay out of its path until it disappears completely. If rooted, you will be pulled in and hit by the follow-up, so use the movement speed from Neeko W Shapesplitter to get out of its path. Swain Q Death's Hand hits with several bolts overlapping at close range, so keep your distance.

Sylas.build: Sylas's main damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Buy Null-Magic Mantle early, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If the healing from Sylas W Kingslayer can disrupt your finish, fit Morellonomicon between core items.
Sylas.combo: The basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root, then Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. When Sylas E Abscond / Abduct is down and you have an opportunity to engage, approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so the landing hits. If the healing from Sylas W Kingslayer could prevent you from finishing him off, apply Grievous Wounds as part of that engage too.
Sylas.escape: Do not go in just because you see the first dash from Sylas E Abscond / Abduct; wait for a chance after dodging the chains that follow. Sylas can also move with Sylas W Kingslayer, so do not chase just because only one ability is down. In particular, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs before Sylas E Abscond / Abduct comes back up.
Sylas.fight: Start a trade when you have an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and if there is no angle, chip away at his health with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Right after Sylas engages with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and deal damage before he can heal with Sylas W Kingslayer. If Sylas still has a mobility skill available, do not rush in with Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Sylas.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to create an easier angle to hit, and follow a hit with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. Watch for Sylas's engage while Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is on cooldown or misses.
Sylas.phase: After learning Neeko R Pop Blossom, you can combine disguise and root for an engage, and mid game, as your ability power builds, is Neeko's peak. In the late game, you have few options left after using both Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Sylas.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then catch Sylas right after he dives in with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct to create a chance to focus him before he heals with Sylas W Kingslayer. Sylas R Hijack can steal Neeko R Pop Blossom, so watch your distance to avoid giving him range to steal it.
Sylas.watch: With Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, the chains that fly after the first dash are more dangerous than the dash itself. If they hit, Sylas pulls himself to you and knocks you up, so use the movement speed from Neeko W Shapesplitter to dodge the second chain. If you are clipped by Sylas Q Chain Lash, immediately leave the crossing point where it explodes after a delay.

Syndra.build: Survive the early game with a Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Syndra’s main damage, but also watch your total health to prepare for the true damage from Syndra W Force of Will and the execute from Syndra R Unleashed Power.
Syndra.combo: Your basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. If Syndra E Scatter the Weak is down, use Neeko P Inherent Glamour to disguise yourself and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko's landing hits her.
Syndra.escape: Syndra E Scatter the Weak has a long cooldown and is her only self-defense tool, so immediately after she uses it is your window to engage. Approach while staying out of the line where Syndra Q Dark Sphere is placed, then root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so she can’t escape.
Syndra.fight: While Syndra E Scatter the Weak is available, avoid the line of spheres and poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered attack. Right after Syndra E Scatter the Weak is used, root her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and follow up with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks.
Syndra.laning: Syndra Q Dark Sphere, Syndra W Force of Will, and Syndra E Scatter the Weak are skillshots, so get boots early and walk out of the spots she telegraphs. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to try to hit her, and save it when there’s no angle, poking with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s third empowered attack instead.
Syndra.phase: Neeko has low armor early, so dodge Syndra’s skillshots and wait for a safe angle for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. In the late game, Neeko loses power after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so follow your engage order and reassess your distance when you see the effects of Syndra’s empowered abilities.
Syndra.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Syndra E Scatter the Weak is down or the enemy is held in place by an allied engage. Avoid entering areas with several Syndra Q Dark Spheres, since Syndra R Unleashed Power deals more damage there.
Syndra.watch: Move away from areas where several Dark Spheres are set up, since Syndra R Unleashed Power deals more damage there and can execute you at low health.

Talon.build: Build Cloth Armor early to survive, and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Talon's damage is physical, so build armor first, and add health to counter lethality. Neeko's magic damage is easily blocked by Talon's high magic resistance, so include penetration too.
Talon.combo: Root Talon with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs sent through minions, then use Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. After Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy is down, close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with E to land as you come down.
Talon.escape: The moment after you make Talon use Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy is Neeko's chance to engage. If you have confirmed Talon R Shadow Assault is also down, counterattack in a spot where he cannot escape with stealth.
Talon.fight: Start a trade when you have an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If E is unavailable, watch for Talon's engage and poke with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter. Right after Talon uses Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to counterattack.
Talon.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions, and be careful of Talon's engage if it misses. If Talon roams, share his position and ward the jungle paths.
Talon.phase: Talon's influence falls off in the late game, but Neeko also loses power after using E and R, so follow the engage order.
Talon.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and layer crowd control with your allies if Talon jumps in. After the enemy is caught, finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom, and do not enter the enemy team alone while preparing.
Talon.watch: If both the outgoing and returning hits of Talon W Rake connect, stacks of Talon P Blade's End build up, so if the first hit connects, move out of its return path. While Talon R Shadow Assault is available, he can escape with stealth, so do not chase recklessly.

Taric.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Taric's main damage is magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the healing from Taric Q Starlight's Touch can undo your burst damage, fit Morellonomicon between core items.
Taric.combo: The basic order is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, cast Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. To engage, approach disguised with Neeko P Inherent Glamour, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then land your ultimate on an enemy held in place by Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or allied crowd control. If Taric R Cosmic Radiance's damage immunity is already active, stop dealing damage and keep them rooted or stunned, then attack again the moment the immunity ends.
Taric.escape: The moment after Taric E Dazzle is down is your chance to engage. Taric has no skill to create distance himself, so if you have an angle to catch him, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and close the gap with Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Taric.fight: After dodging Taric E Dazzle sideways, keep your range and trade. Hit a champion with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter, and if Neeko E Tangle-Barbs hits, follow with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. Keeping your distance so Taric cannot stick to his basic attack target also slows how quickly he can recast abilities with Taric P Bravado.
Taric.laning: Early on, do not trade basic attacks up close with Taric; poke from range. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to aim for a hit. If there is no angle for a root, do not force it; wait while chipping away at his health with the empowered basic attack from Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Taric.phase: In the late game, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Taric.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught up in an allied engage. If Taric R Cosmic Radiance's damage immunity activates, stop dealing damage and keep the enemy in place with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or Neeko R Pop Blossom. Resume your damage the moment the immunity ends.
Taric.watch: If you see the warning for Taric E Dazzle, move sideways to dodge it. Do not unload damage while the damage immunity from Taric R Cosmic Radiance is active.

Thresh.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Since Thresh’s main damage is magic, Neeko should build magic resistance first.
Thresh.combo: Your basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then hold the enemy in place with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control so Neeko’s ultimate hits them when she lands.
Thresh.escape: Right after dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence, you have an opportunity to close the distance, but Thresh W Dark Passage can extract the enemy if it is still available. If Thresh W Dark Passage has also been used and has not come off cooldown yet, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root the enemy with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Thresh.fight: Trade with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs when Thresh walks forward to collect souls. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is unavailable, don’t force an engage; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered attack instead.
Thresh.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow and travel faster, making it easier to root Thresh. Use two basic attacks on minions, then hit Thresh with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s third empowered attack. Don’t approach in a straight line while Thresh Q Death Sentence is available.
Thresh.phase: Later, you have little to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Thresh.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by an ally’s engage. If Thresh W Dark Passage has been thrown, decide whether to finish the target immediately or back off. If you’re trapped in Thresh R The Box, choose an escape direction and have your toughest ally break through one wall.
Thresh.watch: Thresh Q Death Sentence has a long windup, but getting hit lets him engage, so especially when moving up for a last hit, change direction left or right to dodge it. Move out of the line between Thresh and his ally so Thresh E Flay can’t pull you toward them.

TwistedFate.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game to withstand Twisted Fate’s magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots, and prioritize magic resistance.
TwistedFate.combo: Your basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. Once Twisted Fate W Pick a Card’s gold card is down, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s ultimate hits him when she lands.
TwistedFate.escape: The moment Twisted Fate W Pick a Card’s gold card is used is an opportunity to engage.
TwistedFate.fight: While Twisted Fate W Pick a Card’s gold card is available, don’t force an approach; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered attack. When he has used the gold card or is holding a blue or red card, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and deal damage.
TwistedFate.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to try to hit and root the enemy for longer. When there’s no angle, wait while using Neeko W Shapesplitter’s third attack on the enemy, and stand behind minions to reduce damage from Twisted Fate Q Wild Cards.
TwistedFate.phase: Neeko has low armor early, so trade carefully while waiting for an opening to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. Later, you have little to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order even more carefully.
TwistedFate.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Twisted Fate W Pick a Card’s gold card is used or an ally’s engage catches the enemy. If you see Twisted Fate R Destiny being cast within range, interrupt his movement with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or Neeko R Pop Blossom.
TwistedFate.watch: If Twisted Fate has locked in a gold card with Twisted Fate W Pick a Card, one basic attack will stun you, so stay outside his basic attack range.

Veigar.build: Veigar’s damage is mostly magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Survive the early game with a Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Veigar.combo: Your basic combo is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs thrown through minions, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. If Veigar E Event Horizon is down, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root Veigar with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s ultimate hits him when she lands.
Veigar.escape: When Veigar E Event Horizon is down, you have an opportunity to engage. If you’re trapped, move inside without touching the edge, then use Neeko R Pop Blossom as you leave. If health drops below half, don’t engage; get out of range of Veigar R Primordial Burst.
Veigar.fight: Keep moving to dodge Veigar W Dark Matter while poking with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered attack. If Veigar E Event Horizon is down, close the distance, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and attack. Don’t force an engage while Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is unavailable.
Veigar.laning: Pressure Veigar early, before he stacks up, to disrupt his farming and poke. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to hit Veigar, then follow up with Neeko Q Blooming Burst if it lands. Don’t use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s third empowered attack on a minion; hit Veigar with it.
Veigar.phase: Early on, Neeko has an opportunity to pressure Veigar, who has low armor and no mobility. Later, Veigar keeps growing stronger through Veigar P Phenomenal Evil Power stacks, so choose your engage order carefully.
Veigar.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and check whether Veigar E Event Horizon has been used. Finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Veigar is caught by an ally’s engage. If you use Neeko R Pop Blossom first and go in alone, you can be attacked while it prepares.
Veigar.watch: Veigar E Event Horizon stuns you when you cross its edge. If you’re trapped inside, don’t run into the edge; move within the zone and watch Veigar W Dark Matter’s ground indicator to dodge sideways. Veigar Q Baleful Strike passes through only the first two units it hits, so stand behind minions to avoid it. If health is below half, get out of range of Veigar R Primordial Burst, which grows stronger based on missing health.

Velkoz.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Vel'Koz’s main magic damage, but Vel'Koz P Organic Deconstruction and Vel'Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray deal true damage that resistance can’t block, so your priority is to avoid being hit by consecutive abilities.
Velkoz.combo: Your basic sequence is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. To engage, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then hold Vel'Koz in place with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control so Neeko’s ultimate hits him when she lands.
Velkoz.escape: Right after Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption misses is your opportunity to engage. Vel'Koz has no mobility, so close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, but account for Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption knocking you back if you get very close.
Velkoz.fight: After dodging Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption, close the distance. Root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use an empowered attack. If there’s no angle to root him, don’t force it; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s passive instead.
Velkoz.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to try to root Vel'Koz. Hitting both the wave and Vel'Koz with Neeko Q Blooming Burst lets you clear the wave and poke at the same time. Watch for Vel'Koz’s counterattack after missing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Velkoz.phase: Later, you have little to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Velkoz.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Vel'Koz is caught by an ally’s engage. When Vel'Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, first look for a chance to interrupt it with Neeko R Pop Blossom’s stun; if you can’t interrupt it, move away in a direction that breaks vision.
Velkoz.watch: Even if you dodge the main beam of Vel'Koz Q Plasma Fission, you can still be hit by the beams that split off to either side, so move toward Vel'Koz or behind the beams after they pass instead of dodging only sideways. If Vel'Koz W Void Rift and Vel'Koz E Tectonic Disruption also hit in succession, Vel'Koz P Organic Deconstruction’s true damage triggers, so back off and let the stacks wear off when they’re applied.

Vex.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game to withstand Vex’s magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots and prioritize magic resistance.
Vex.combo: Root Vex with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs thrown through minions, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then hold her in place with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs or an ally’s crowd control so Neeko’s ultimate hits her when she lands.
Vex.escape: Right after Vex uses Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s Doom on the wave or to poke, you have an opening to engage. If Vex W Personal Space’s shield is down too, catch her with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Vex.fight: If there’s no angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, wait while poking with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s third empowered attack. Once Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s Doom is consumed and Vex W Personal Space’s shield is down, start the fight with a root.
Vex.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make the root last longer. Hitting both the wave and Vex with Neeko Q Blooming Burst lets you clear the wave and poke at the same time. After missing your root, don’t force a trade, since it gives Vex an opening to engage.
Vex.phase: Later, you have little to do after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Vex.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Vex is caught by an ally’s engage. An ally marked by Vex R Shadow Surge should move toward the team so everyone can absorb Vex’s dash together. Move low-health allies out of Vex’s range first to prevent Vex R Shadow Surge from recasting.
Vex.watch: Don’t dive with Neeko R Pop Blossom while Vex P Doom 'n Gloom’s Doom indicator is showing. Vex E Looming Darkness grows larger over distance, so if you’re already in range, dodge a short distance to the side instead of retreating far backward. If Vex R Shadow Surge hits you, move toward your allies to prepare for the follow-up dash.

Viktor.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game to withstand Viktor’s magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots, and use Neeko W Shapesplitter’s movement speed to escape Viktor W Gravity Field.
Viktor.combo: Your basic sequence is to root with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then use basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root Viktor with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s ultimate hits him when she lands.
Viktor.escape: When Viktor W Gravity Field is down, you have an opportunity to engage. Viktor has no dash, so close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom then and root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If Viktor W Gravity Field is still available, don’t keep trading inside its area.
Viktor.fight: Pressure Viktor from the start, before he builds up upgrade stacks. When there’s an angle for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, root him and trade with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks; if there’s no angle, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s empowered attack.
Viktor.laning: When Viktor uses Viktor E Hextech Ray on the wave, don’t stand in a line with the minions. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to root Viktor, then hit both the wave and Viktor with Neeko Q Blooming Burst to clear the wave and poke at the same time. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, don’t force an engage.
Viktor.phase: Early, before Viktor builds up Viktor P Glorious Evolution stacks, is the best time to pressure him. Later, Viktor’s accumulated growth makes him stronger, so carefully plan the order in which you engage with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Viktor.teamfight: From the back line, first use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to catch Viktor or start the fight. Finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after an ally’s engage catches the enemy, and don’t stay inside Viktor W Gravity Field.
Viktor.watch: Viktor E Hextech Ray travels in a straight line, so don’t stand in line with the minion wave; step aside to dodge it. Leave Viktor W Gravity Field immediately to avoid being stunned, and don’t keep fighting where Viktor R Arcane Storm is placed.

Vladimir.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Vladimir’s main damage is magic and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. If his healing is enough to undo Neeko’s burst damage, fit Morellonomicon in between your core items.
Vladimir.combo: After making Vladimir use Vladimir W Sanguine Pool, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then attack with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. To engage with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour and approach, prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs so Neeko’s ultimate hits him when she lands.
Vladimir.escape: The moment Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ends is Neeko’s opportunity to engage. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs catches him then, Vladimir has no way to create distance on his own. Vladimir moves more slowly while charging Vladimir E Tides of Blood, which can give you an opportunity to close the distance.
Vladimir.fight: Early on, look for an angle for Neeko E Tangle-Barbs; if you can’t hit it, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter’s third empowered attack. Make Vladimir use Vladimir W Sanguine Pool first, then root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs as it ends and follow up with Neeko Q Blooming Burst. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs misses, it’s hard to deal guaranteed damage, so don’t force an engage.
Vladimir.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to improve its hit chance and enhance its rooting effect. Hitting the wave with Neeko Q Blooming Burst lets you poke while triggering chain explosions from killing minions.
Vladimir.phase: Later, you have few options left after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so plan your engage order carefully.
Vladimir.teamfight: Start from the back line with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then use Neeko R Pop Blossom with your allies’ engage after Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down. If you’re infected by Vladimir R Hemoplague, step back and re-engage after it wears off. If several allies are hit by Vladimir R Hemoplague, Vladimir’s healing increases, so don’t group inside its area.
Vladimir.watch: Vladimir W Sanguine Pool dodges incoming projectiles and breaks target locks, so make him use it before using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom. When Vladimir E Tides of Blood is charged, put minions between you or move out of range. If you’re affected by Vladimir R Hemoplague, back off until it wears off, since you’ll take increased damage.

Xerath.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Xerath deals mostly magic damage, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Xerath.combo: Your basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs root → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. When Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down and you go in with your ultimate, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour as you approach, then prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom and use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to root him so the landing hits.
Xerath.escape: Xerath has no mobility, so the moment after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down is your window to engage. Close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom then, and hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to keep him from escaping.
Xerath.fight: Close the distance just after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. Xerath has no mobility, so root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then hit him with Neeko Q Blooming Burst and basic attacks. If you don't have an angle to root him, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's empowered basic attack and wait.
Xerath.laning: Xerath Q Arcanopulse can hit you even behind minions, so move to the side when you see him charge it, and look for a chance to approach while Xerath is slowed. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow and travel faster, making it easier to root Xerath. Farm while avoiding heavy damage; when Xerath runs out of mana, push the lane and call your jungler.
Xerath.phase: Early on, respect Xerath's long range, avoid heavy damage, and farm. Later, Neeko has fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Xerath.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, and don't go in alone with Neeko R Pop Blossom while crowd control such as Xerath E Shocking Orb is still available. Finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by your allies' engage. When you see Xerath R Rite of the Arcane's cast animation, dodge first, or if you can engage, go toward Xerath while he can't move.
Xerath.watch: If Xerath E Shocking Orb stuns you, you can take his full follow-up, so watch out most for that shot. Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so when you see him charge it, change direction and dodge well to the side. Start dodging as soon as you see Xerath R Rite of the Arcane's cast animation.

Yasuo.build: Early on, buy Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Since Yasuo's main damage is physical, armor is the priority for Neeko. Armor doesn't block the magic damage from Yasuo E Sweeping Blade.
Yasuo.combo: Break Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer's shield first, then attack in this order: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. Root Yasuo with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs before placing Neeko Q Blooming Burst to make the follow-up explosion easier to hit. If Yasuo W Wind Wall blocks your path, save your key abilities and go around it or wait for it to disappear.
Yasuo.escape: Right after Yasuo throws his tornado is your chance to go in. Don't engage just because Yasuo E Sweeping Blade is down; look for an opening with crowd control before Yasuo R Last Breath comes back. When closing the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom, land Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to keep him from escaping.
Yasuo.fight: First break Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer's shield with light poke, then start trading. Right after Yasuo throws his tornado, he briefly has no way to knock you up, so look for an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs. If you don't have an angle, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's third empowered basic attack and wait.
Yasuo.laning: Manage the wave so a thin wave pushes toward Neeko, reducing the number of minions Yasuo can use to dash in with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade. Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle that sends it through minions to aim for a hit and root. Missing Neeko E Tangle-Barbs gives Yasuo an opportunity to engage, so save it when you don't have an angle.
Yasuo.phase: Later, Neeko has fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Yasuo.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Yasuo is caught by your allies' engage. Disguising yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour as you approach can hide Neeko R Pop Blossom's windup, but account for the possibility that the spot where you start the windup may be revealed. Going in alone first can get you caught during the windup, so leave room to use Neeko W Shapesplitter.
Yasuo.watch: Yasuo Q Steel Tempest has a narrow hitbox, so move to the side as he approaches to dodge it. After he hits it twice in a row, his next Yasuo Q Steel Tempest knocks you up as a tornado, so watch for the sound and visual effect and dodge early. If there are minions, Yasuo can approach with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade, so watch the wave that can serve as his stepping stones.

Yone.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can leave the warned attack area. Yone deals a mix of physical and magic damage, so if you build resistances, account for both types. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on max health, so avoid choices that only add a lot of health.
Yone.combo: After Yone goes in, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then land an empowered basic attack. Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and travels faster, and its root lasts longer, when it passes through minions first, making this sequence easier to complete.
Yone.escape: Don't go in just because Yone Q Mortal Steel is down. Yone E Soul Unbound and R Fate Sealed are also mobility tools, so look for an engage opportunity especially before Yone R Fate Sealed comes back. If Yone dives in first with E Soul Unbound, you can prevent his return with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Yone.fight: Keep your distance while Yone's tornado Q is ready; if you don't have an angle, poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's third empowered basic attack. If Yone goes in with Yone E Soul Unbound, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to prevent his return, then follow the root with Neeko Q Blooming Burst.
Yone.laning: Use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle that sends it through minions, and watch out for Yone's engage after it misses.
Yone.phase: Later, Neeko has fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
Yone.teamfight: Start from the backline with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, then finish with Neeko R Pop Blossom after Yone is rooted or caught by your allies' engage. Spread out from your allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave's shield doesn't grow, and check that you aren't standing alone at the very back of your formation before Yone R Fate Sealed. If Yone E Soul Unbound damages you, account for the extra damage when he returns to his body and get out of range in advance.
Yone.watch: If Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions, his tornado engage is ready, so stay out of range until the stacks expire. Hold Neeko E Tangle-Barbs in case Yone dives in with Yone E Soul Unbound. Yone R Fate Sealed moves him behind the last champion in its path, so check whether you are at the very back of your formation before a team fight.

Zed.build: Early on, hold out by buying Cloth Armor first and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Zed's main damage is physical, and Neeko has low armor, so build armor first.
Zed.combo: Root Zed with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, place Neeko Q Blooming Burst, then land basic attacks.
Zed.escape: Don't go in just because Zed W Living Shadow is down. If Zed R Death Mark is also down and hasn't returned yet, close the distance with Neeko R Pop Blossom and look for a chance to root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs.
Zed.fight: If you don't have an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don't force a fight; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's empowered basic attack.
Zed.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions to make it grow and travel faster, and extend its root. After using two basic attacks on minions, hit Zed with Neeko W Shapesplitter's third empowered basic attack. If you miss the root or have exhausted your abilities, watch out for Zed's engage.
Zed.phase: Later, group with your allies so Zed has no isolated target to pick off, and carefully choose the order in which you use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom.
Zed.teamfight: Hit Neeko R Pop Blossom after the enemy is caught by your allies' engage.
Zed.watch: When Zed goes in with Zed W Living Shadow, watch the shadow's position and move outside Zed E Shadow Slash's slow area. If Zed R Death Mark is on you, root him with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs before he can stack more damage and interrupt his combo.

Zilean.build: Early on, hold out with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zilean deals magic damage, so build magic resistance, but tenacity has the more immediate effect when you're caught by the bomb stun and slow. If Zilean R Chronoshift's healing can undo the explosion damage, fit Morellonomicon in among your core items.
Zilean.combo: Your basic trade is Neeko E Tangle-Barbs → Neeko Q Blooming Burst → basic attacks. Rooting Zilean with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs through minions makes Neeko Q Blooming Burst easier to hit. For an ultimate engage, disguise yourself with Neeko P Inherent Glamour as you approach, then prepare Neeko R Pop Blossom and use Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to root him so the landing hits.
Zilean.escape: Zilean has no mobility, so close the distance after Zilean E Time Warp is down. Also watch out for the stun made by two Zilean Q Time Bombs; if the first bomb attaches, move away from your allies and out of its blast radius. When you engage, root Zilean with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs to keep him from escaping.
Zilean.fight: If you don't have an angle to hit Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, don't force it; poke with Neeko W Shapesplitter's third empowered basic attack. If Zilean E Time Warp is still available, going in alone can leave you caught by the slow and bomb combo, so don't rush your engage.
Zilean.laning: Throw Neeko E Tangle-Barbs at an angle that sends it through minions to target Zilean.
Zilean.phase: Neeko is strong in the mid game as her ability power builds, and later she has fewer options after using Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and Neeko R Pop Blossom, so choose your engage order carefully.
